referents.why: 'your staff' is inside the commanded words Moses is to speak to Aaron; the addressee of those words is Aaron (w7), masculine singular agrees.
'say to Aaron' is God's command to Moses; the implied you is the one commanded, Moses. The builder's Aaron is the addressee of the words Moses is to say, not of this command.
referents.category: implied subject of the outer command

referents.why: 'stretch out' belongs to the words Moses is told to say to Aaron, so the implied you is Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 'strike' is in the same commanded words; the implied you is Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: the weqatal 'it will become gnats' is third masculine singular; the thing struck, the dust (w15), is what becomes gnats. The act decides, not the nearest noun.
referents.category: implied subject of a result clause

links.why: cl0 is the frame of God's speech and comes before the commanded clauses; cl3 is inside the speech, so a then-link back to the frame is backward and crosses the speech boundary.
plain waw joining two commands at one level; the conjunction supports it.
the weqatal says what the command brings about; that is the result link, not a plain sequence.
imperative, then waw + third-person weqatal saying what will come of it (R4).
God says, and what is said is the clause 'say to Aaron' (R1).
'say to Aaron' introduces a collection of commands joined by waw; content points at the imperative group (R1).

groups.why: God (the LORD) speaks to Moses; the commanded turn is nested as a part (speech nests), so cl1 is the frame of turn1 rather than a separate part of God's turn.
groups.category: outer speech with nested commanded turn

groups.why: the commanded words are spoken by Moses, the one commanded to speak them, to Aaron (R2); the sender was a slot and is replaced by the candidate Moses.
commands joined by 'and' at one level are one imperative group with several command members; the weqatal is its effect.
the strike command belongs to the single collection imp2; a second group for it duplicates the first.
